candidates.title: Reaching Agreement Among Reasoning LLM Agents
candidates.abstract: Multi-agent systems have extended the capability of agentic AI. Instead of single inference passes, multiple agents perform collective reasoning to derive high quality answers. However, existing multi-agent orchestration relies on static heuristic workflows such as fixed loop limits and barrier synchronization. These ad-hoc approaches waste computational resources, incur high latency due to stragglers, and risk finalizing transient agreements. We argue that reliable multi-agent reasoning requires a formal foundation analogous to classical distributed consensus problem. To that end, we propose a formal model of the multi-agent refinement problem. The model includes definitions of the correctness guarantees and formal semantics of agent reasoning. We then introduce Aegean, a consensus protocol designed for stochastic reasoning agents that solves multi-agent refinement. We implement the protocol in Aegean-Serve, a consensus-aware serving engine that performs incremental quorum detection across concurrent agent executions, enabling early termination when sufficient agents converge. Evaluation using four mathematical reasoning benchmarks shows that Aegean provides provable safety and liveness guarantees while reducing latency by 1.2--20$\times$ compared to state-of-the-art baselines, maintaining answer quality within 2.5%. Consistent gains across both local GPU deployments and commercial API providers validate that consensus-based orchestration eliminates straggler delays without sacrificing correctness.
candidates.reason: 推論LLMエージェント群の合意形成をAegean-Serveという合意対応サービングエンジンで実装し、増分クォーラム検出による早期終了で遅延を1.2〜20倍削減するため、分散推論サービングへの直接貢献として採用とする。

candidates.title: Fast Graph Vector Search via Hardware Acceleration and Delayed-Synchronization Traversal
candidates.abstract: Vector search systems are indispensable in large language model (LLM) serving, search engines, and recommender systems, where minimizing online search latency is essential. Among various algorithms, graph-based vector search (GVS) is particularly popular due to its high search performance and quality. However, reducing GVS latency by intra-query parallelization remains challenging due to limitations imposed by both existing hardware architectures (CPUs and GPUs) and the inherent difficulty of parallelizing graph traversals. To efficiently serve low-latency GVS, we co-design hardware and algorithm by proposing Falcon and Delayed-Synchronization Traversal (DST). Falcon is a hardware GVS accelerator that implements efficient GVS operators, pipelines these operators, and reduces memory accesses by tracking search states with an on-chip Bloom filter. DST is an efficient graph traversal algorithm that simultaneously improves search performance and quality by relaxing traversal orders to maximize accelerator utilization. Evaluation across various graphs and datasets shows that Falcon, prototyped on FPGAs, together with DST, achieves up to 4.3X and 19.5X lower latency and up to 8.0X and 26.9X improvements in energy efficiency over CPU- and GPU-based GVS systems.
candidates.reason: グラフ型ベクトル探索をLLMサービングの低遅延要件向けにハードウェア加速器Falconと遅延同期走査DSTで協調設計し、FPGA試作で最大19.5倍の遅延削減を示すため、推論基盤の検索コンポーネントへの直接貢献として採用とする。

candidates.title: HiSVD: Principled Low-Rank Approximation of LLMs via Hierarchical Modeling of Information Capacity and Spectral Structure
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.reason: LLMの低ランク近似におけるランク配分を情報容量とスペクトル冗長性の階層モデルで決めるHiSVDは、ハードウェア非依存のLLM圧縮手法として推論時のモデルサイズと計算削減へ直接貢献するため採用とする。

candidates.title: SPARE: Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy for Efficient MoEs
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale model capacity efficiently, yet their substantial memory footprint poses a major barrier to deployment. Expert pruning reduces this footprint, but most methods focus on which experts to remove and prune every layer equally. We propose SPARE (Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy), a training-free, selector-agnostic method that decides how many experts to remove from each layer using routing entropy, the entropy of tokens'normalized Top-K gate weights on calibration data. When a token's gate weight is spread evenly, removing one active expert discards little of it, so SPARE prunes layers with more diffuse routing more aggressively. A perturbation bound under random pruning formalizes this intuition, and controlled interventions with a fixed selector link concentrated routing to larger output changes. With the same selector and budget, SPARE improves average accuracy over uniform allocation on Mixtral, Qwen3, and DeepSeek models, especially at high pruning ratios. At 50% expert pruning, it raises the eight-task average of Qwen3-30B-A3B from 57.2% to 63.8%, and the math, code, and science average of DeepSeek-R1 from 80.1 to 82.8.
candidates.reason: MoEの層別ルーティングエントロピーに基づき訓練不要で専門家プルーニング量を配分するSPAREは、MixtralやQwen3、DeepSeek-R1で50%プルーニング時の精度を改善し、MoE推論のメモリフットプリント削減へ直接貢献するため採用とする。

candidates.title: ChipChat: Low-Latency Cascaded Conversational Agent in MLX
candidates.abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has transformed spoken dialog systems, yet the optimal architecture for real-time on-device voice agents remains an open question. While end-to-end approaches promise theoretical advantages, cascaded systems (CSs) continue to outperform them in language understanding tasks, despite being constrained by sequential processing latency. In this work, we introduce ChipChat, a novel low-latency CS that overcomes traditional bottlenecks through architectural innovations and streaming optimizations. Our system integrates streaming (a) conversational speech recognition with mixture-of-experts, (b) state-action augmented LLM, (c) text-to-speech synthesis, (d) neural vocoder, and (e) speaker modeling. Implemented using MLX, ChipChat achieves subsecond response latency on a Mac Studio without dedicated GPUs, while preserving user privacy through complete on-device processing. Our work shows that strategically redesigned CSs can overcome their historical latency limitations, offering a promising path forward for practical voice-based AI agents.
candidates.reason: MLX実装のカスケード型会話エージェントChipChatは、ストリーミングASRやLLM、TTSをMac Studio上でGPUなしにサブ秒応答で動かすオンデバイス低遅延推論システムを具体的に示しており、推論基盤への直接貢献が確認できるため採用とする。
